title: Dairy-Free Apple Pie Cupcakes
shortDescription: These dairy-free apple pie cupcakes take 25 minutes to prep and 18 minutes to bake, with a warm apple compote center and vanilla swirl frosting.
description: These cupcakes taste like apple pie in a small, easy to eat form. A soft cinnamon cake wraps around a spoonful of homemade apple compote, so every bite has a warm, fruity center. I made these for a fall potluck where two guests could not have dairy. Nobody guessed the frosting was dairy-free, they just kept asking for the recipe. The vanilla swirl frosting uses plant butter and a splash of non-dairy milk, so it whips up light and holds its shape. A dust of cinnamon on top brings back that classic pie smell. This recipe works well for Thanksgiving tables or any time you want fall flavor without the pie crust.
ingredients: 1 tsp ground cinnamon, plus extra for dusting
1 1/2 cups peeled, diced apples (about 2 medium apples)
1/3 cup dairy-free shortening or extra plant butter
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin tin with 12 paper liners.
In a small saucepan, cook diced apples, brown sugar, water, and lemon juice over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft. Set the compote aside to cool.
In a bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt together.
In a large bowl, beat dairy-free butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla extract.
Alternate adding the flour mix and almond milk to the batter, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
Spoon a small amount of batter into each liner, add 1 teaspoon of cooled apple compote to the center, then top with more batter to cover.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick in the cake part comes out clean. Cool completely before frosting.
For the frosting, beat dairy-free shortening or plant butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar one cup at a time with the vanilla extract.
Pipe the vanilla frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake, then dust with cinnamon.
tips: Use a firm baking apple like Granny Smith or Honeycrisp so the compote holds its shape.
Cool the apple compote fully before adding it to the batter, or it will melt the cake too fast.
If your frosting feels too soft, chill it for 10 minutes before piping.
Dust the cinnamon right before serving so it stays visible and does not sink into the frosting.

faq.question: Can I use canned apple pie filling instead of homemade compote?
faq.answer: Yes, chop the apple pieces smaller so they fit inside the cupcake center. Drain excess liquid first so the batter does not turn soggy.

faq.question: What dairy-free butter works best for the frosting?
faq.answer: A stick-style plant butter with 80 percent fat gives the best texture. Spreadable tub butters can make the frosting too soft to pipe.

faq.question: Why did my apple center sink to the bottom?
faq.answer: This happens if the compote is too warm or the batter layer underneath is too thin. Let the compote cool fully and use a solid base layer of batter first.

faq.question: Can I make these nut-free too?
faq.answer: Yes, swap the almond milk for oat milk or soy milk. Both work well in this batter and keep it fully dairy-free.

conclusion: These dairy-free apple pie cupcakes bring fall flavor to any table without dairy on the label. The apple compote center keeps them moist for days, and the vanilla swirl frosting makes them look bakery ready.
